description.p: Planck is an open source code editor written in Rust with native GUI and GPU rendering. It is derived from the Lapce editor.

ul.li: Modal Editing (Vim like) support as first class citizen (can be turned off as well)
Built-in LSP (Language Server Protocol) support: configure a language server command and get completion, diagnostics and code actions
Built-in terminal, so you can execute commands in your workspace, without leaving Planck.

screenshot.caption: Rust source code file opened in Planck

description.p: Binary files shown as a hex dump are colored, and the unsaved-changes dialog is clearer and asks about every file when closing several tabs.
Planck guesses the language of Untitled files and files without an extension from their content, and syntax highlighting is fixed and extended across many languages.
Planck makes no network connections: the updater is gone, syntax highlighting is built in, and the markdown preview no longer loads remote images.
Planck has one window, unsaved Untitled files are never lost, and the planck command opens files from a terminal.
Untitled files, and files opened without a folder, stay open when you open a folder or space.
Help only offers an update once its download is ready and shows why an update failed, and the macOS app runs natively on Intel Macs too.
Binary files like GIFs open as a read-only hex view with offsets, hex bytes and ASCII, searchable with Find.

A markdown Rich view that edits in place with live formatting (tables, images, front matter, links, task checkboxes, GitHub alerts), a minimap that replaces the scroll bar with a button to switch between them, and Bash highlighting for shell dotfiles.

Mouse support in the terminal (apps like vim, htop and tmux, middle-click paste, copy on select), error messages in the hover, and space explorer additions: an add-folder button, Open in Terminal, and open folders remembered across restarts.
Sessions survive a crash or forced quit, files-only windows keep their panels, and a double click on the top bar maximizes the window on Wayland.
A Git Graph panel that draws the history of every branch, notifications when a language server is missing or stops, and a fix for language servers stopping a few seconds after start.
New MkiP color themes based on the Monokai Pro filters, and bracket pair colorization on by default.
System monitor in the status bar, drag files from the explorer into an editor group, and every opened file keeps its own tab.
Fixes a new Untitled file replacing a restored one, double click the tab bar to create a file, and a Linux icon sized like other apps.
Menu bar inside the window on macOS, syntax highlighting on Linux arm64, Linux packages update through the package manager.
First Planck release, forked from Lapce 0.4.6.
